front_blocks.md: Why can gases be compressed but solids cannot?
**(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: In gases, particles are far apart with large empty spaces between them, so they can be pushed closer together.
In solids, particles are already close together with no room to compress further.

front_blocks.md: What does kinetic theory state?

back_blocks.md: Kinetic theory states that all matter is made of particles in constant motion, and that the properties of each state of matter depend on the arrangement and movement of those particles.

cards.front_md: What does kinetic theory state?

Both solids and liquids have particles that are close together.

front_blocks.md: What is the arrangement and motion of particles in a gas?

back_blocks.md: Gas particles are in a random arrangement, far apart, and move rapidly in all directions. They exert pressure on their container by colliding with the walls.

front_blocks.md: Why do gases exert pressure on the walls of their container?
**(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: Gas particles move rapidly and in all directions, colliding with the container walls. Each collision exerts a small force, and the combined effect of many collisions per second is experienced as pressure.

front_blocks.md: How does the particle model explain why solids have a higher density than gases?
**(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: Solid particles are packed close together in a regular arrangement with little empty space, so a given volume contains many particles. Gas particles are far apart, so the same volume contains far fewer particles, giving gases a much lower density.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Boiling and evaporation both only occur at the boiling point of a liquid.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Boiling occurs at a fixed boiling point and produces bubbles throughout the liquid.
Evaporation can occur at any temperature below the boiling point and takes place only at the surface.

**False.**

back_blocks.md: During evaporation, only the most **energetic** particles at the surface of a liquid have enough energy to **escape** the liquid.

cards.back_md: During evaporation, only the most **energetic** particles at the surface of a liquid have enough energy to **escape** the liquid.

front_blocks.md: Why does evaporation cause the temperature of a liquid to fall?

back_blocks.md: During evaporation, the most energetic particles escape from the surface of the liquid. This reduces the **average kinetic energy** of the remaining particles, so the temperature of the liquid falls.

back_blocks.md: Boiling occurs at a fixed **boiling point** throughout the bulk of the liquid, forming bubbles.
Evaporation occurs at any temperature at the **surface** of the liquid only, as the most energetic particles escape.

back_blocks.md: During melting, all the energy supplied is used to **break the forces** holding particles in fixed positions. No energy goes into increasing the kinetic energy of particles, so the temperature remains **constant** until all the solid has melted.

front_blocks.md: What is diffusion?

back_blocks.md: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a region of **higher concentration** to a region of **lower concentration**. It occurs due to the random motion of particles and requires no energy input.

front_blocks.md: In the ammonia and hydrogen chloride experiment, why does the white ring of ammonium chloride form closer to the hydrogen chloride end?

back_blocks.md: NH3 has a **lower *****M*****r** (17) than HCl (36.5), so NH3 particles move faster and diffuse further along the tube. The two gases meet closer to the HCl end, where the white ring of ammonium chloride forms.

front_blocks.md: Why does diffusion occur without any energy input?

back_blocks.md: Diffusion occurs because particles are already in **constant random motion** due to their kinetic energy. No additional energy is needed — random particle movement naturally produces a net flow from regions of higher to lower concentration.
